decisions.text: type stacked_bar_100: fractions of the total are the message, but the audience objects to pies: a 100 % stacked bar (G1.40, D-39)
scale 0–100 by 20: each total 100 %, its parts in % of it (R7-30, G7.32)
one total, Donations, stacked from its 5 parts

stacking order from the base: Mrs. Smith, Mrs. Jones, Mr. & Mrs. Perez, The Chetley Family, Ms. Flaherty (Mrs. Smith, the parts the message names, at the base, where they are read precisely; the others largest first; G7.31, D-26 (b))
each part in one colour and one place in every total: Mrs. Smith (slot 1), Mrs. Jones (slot 2), Mr. & Mrs. Perez (slot 3), The Chetley Family (slot 4), Ms. Flaherty (slot 5) (G4.22)
one total: one stack, standing upright (07 §5.4), its parts named beside it: vertical stacked bars
5 values against 6 scale labels: whichever puts fewer numbers on the chart (G2.18): the values labelled directly, the value scale and its gridlines removed, the zero line kept as the baseline
value labels as a set, one magnitude and one number of decimals, the prefix and suffix on each: 24%, 23%, 20%, 18%, 15% (G6.16, G7.4)
each value before its part's name beside the stack: the text grey does not read on the parts' colours at 4.5 : 1 inside them (G7.4, G6.5)
the unit's description on its own line above the plot: “Share of total donations”; the labels carry its prefix, suffix and magnitude

each part named beside the stack, level with the middle of its segment, top to bottom as stacked: Ms. Flaherty, The Chetley Family, Mr. & Mrs. Perez, Mrs. Jones, Mrs. Smith (their values before them) (G5.4, D-31 (c))
highlighted in the strong shade of their colour: Donations (Mrs. Smith); the others keep their colour
